notes: Round-3 composition, fixing round 2's generalization_accuracy_floor regression (r2: 95.5% plausible_fabrication safety cp95-lower but only 81.3% held-out generalization decision accuracy, down from r1's 93.3%, floor 85% -- see plan elegant-bubbling-coral.md "Round 3"). Diagnosed via a real eval_toolcaller.py --dump-failures run against r2's adapter on the sealed generalization arena: 24/28 mismatches were the model predicting {"decision": "unsupported", "reason_code": "no_matching_tool"} for a REAL held-out-family tool whose full schema WAS present in available_tools -- the exact response shape round 2's fabrication-decoy training taught, misfiring on a target it should have called. Root cause: every round-2 training row using explicit-name-drop phrasing ("use X to...", "call the X tool so we can...") was a decoy (correct answer unsupported); normal synthetic-tool call scenarios never used that phrasing, so the model learned the phrasing pattern itself as weak evidence for refusal. v0/r3 stream and v2-bulk-stream-r2 (round 1's 600 + round 2's 120 fabrication decoys) both unchanged -- neither is what broke, and the decoy rows still teach real, necessary safety behavior. New: 117 freshly-generated explicit-call counterexamples (generate_toolcaller_v2_dataset.py --explicit-call-only, tag v2-explicit-call-counterexample) -- same explicit-name-drop phrasing style as the decoys, but targeting a real or train-pool-synthetic tool that IS in available_tools, expected decision "call". Roughly 1:1 volume against round 2's 120 decoys, directly counterbalancing the phrasing-to-refusal association rather than diluting the safety signal by cutting decoy volume. File-level concatenation of three independently ToolcallerBench-PASSed exports, same honest-composition posture as round 1/round 2's meta files.
